sources.entry: Shairport Sync | AirPlay and AirPlay 2 audio receiver

summary.one_liner: Shairport Sync is an AirPlay audio receiver that plays audio streamed from Apple devices and AirPlay sources on Linux, FreeBSD, macOS and OpenBSD.
summary.what_it_does: Shairport Sync receives audio from AirPlay (classic AirPlay 1) and AirPlay 2 sources and plays it on the local machine. It can output to ALSA, sndio, PipeWire, PulseAudio, macOS CoreAudio, a unix pipe, STDOUT, and has limited libao support. It aims for full audio synchronisation with ALSA, sndio, CoreAudio, PipeWire or PulseAudio, using timestamps and interpolation/resampling (optionally libsoxr). Metadata such as artist, album and cover art can be passed to other programs via pipe, UDP, MQTT, an MPRIS-like interface or D-Bus, and remote control commands like play and pause are supported through those interfaces. It also includes DSP facilities and a volume control with extended range. It does not support AirPlay video or photo streaming.
use_cases: Receive AirPlay audio on a Linux or BSD machine
Turn a Raspberry Pi or headless box into an AirPlay speaker
Play iTunes or Apple Music audio through an ALSA sound card
Feed AirPlay metadata and cover art to home automation via MQTT
Control playback from D-Bus or MPRIS clients
Stream AirPlay audio to a pipe for custom audio processing
how_to_run: See the building guide in the repository for build instructions
Optionally use the Docker image on Docker Hub (see docker/README.md)
Consult CONFIGURATION FLAGS.md to choose build-time features
Consult runtime settings documentation for configuration
Refer to the man page for command line options
notable: Supports both classic AirPlay 1 and AirPlay 2 (with some limitations) builds
Full audio synchronisation with accurate timing on ALSA and sndio
Metadata and remote control via MQTT, MPRIS-like interface and D-Bus
Multichannel (5.1, 7.1) and 24-bit lossless stereo at 48 kHz for AirPlay 2
Runs on modest hardware such as a Raspberry Pi
caveats: Does not support AirPlay video or photo streaming
AirPlay 2 protocols are unofficial and may stop working in future
Designed best for dedicated headless systems with ALSA and a good DAC; sound servers give less accurate timing
Apple Silicon Macs have built-in AirPlay and do not need it
